newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chrysler buys back right to sell in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler buys back right to sell in Europe.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Tuesday it bought back distribution rights for its cars in Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium from the Louwman Group, which has overseen the carmaker's brand in Europe since 1987.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Chrysler said it bought back the import companies in each of the three countries, a move it has also taken in Austria, Argentina, Brazil, France, Italy and Japan during the past 18 months.
"Our goals have always been to grow the Chrysler business in these markets," Chrysler Europe president Timothy Adams said in a statement from the carmaker's European headquarters in Brussels.
Chrysler said the dealer network supporting sales and services of Chrysler and Jeep products in Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium consists of 333 dealers.
Combined sales for 1995 totalled almost 28,000 units.
